To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TNDM, a nonlinear state-space modeling framework, can learn low-dimensional dynamics that are highly correlated with the behaviour of interest, without sacrificing its ability to model neural activity.
we introduce a nonlinear state-space neural population dynamics model that is able to learn latent dynamics that are predictive of behavior.

we introduce TNDM, a nonlinear state-space neural population modeling framework that is capable of learning behaviourally relevant and irrelevant dynamics and can reconstruct neural activity and behavior from the learned dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neural mechanisms underlying decision making and action selection.
the development of new methods to model neural data and how they can be used to better understand brain function and behavior.
the development of new computational tools to analyze neural data and understand neural computations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNDM provides a flexible, interpretable framework for modeling neural dynamics that is able to disentangle sources and predict behaviour from neural activity.
TNDM can be used as a general-purpose model of neural activity that can be used to disentangle sources and types of variability in the neural activity and relate them to the behaviour.
we introduce a novel nonlinear state-space model to jointly model the neural activity and the behavioural variables in the latent space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNDM provides a principled way to model and interpret neural dynamics in relation to the external behaviour.
TNDM provides a principled framework for modeling and interpreting the neural dynamics of behaving animals.
TNDM can be used to model and predict the behaviour from neural recordings in a principled and interpretable way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learned latent dynamics are highly interpretable as they are directly related to behaviour through a linear decoder and are therefore useful for understanding the neural basis of behaviour.
TNDM provides a general framework for modeling neural activity that can be applied to any neural recording task with a behavioural component.
the latent space of neural population dynamics can be structured to reflect both behaviourally relevant and irrelevant components of neural activity.
